svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "How adrenaline works: a GPCR and cAMP."], [1, "Adrenaline binds a G protein-coupled receptor."], [3, "The G protein's \u03b1 subunit swaps GDP for GTP..."], [5.5, "...and moves to activate adenylyl cyclase."], [7.5, "Adenylyl cyclase converts ATP into cAMP, the second messenger."], [10, "cAMP activates protein kinase A: a phosphorylation cascade begins."], [13, "Glycogen phosphorylase breaks glycogen down to glucose."], [17, "The signal is hugely amplified."]]
svg.title: Adrenaline, GPCR and cAMP
svg.desc: Adrenaline binds a G protein-coupled receptor; the G protein alpha subunit exchanges GDP for GTP and activates adenylyl cyclase, which converts ATP to cyclic AMP; cAMP activates protein kinase A, starting a phosphorylation cascade that activates glycogen phosphorylase, breaking glycogen into glucose which leaves the liver cell.
svg.text: Adrenaline: a G protein-coupled receptor and cAMP

g.data-info: A transmembrane receptor crossing the membrane seven times. Binding changes its shape.
An amine hormone. It binds a G protein-coupled receptor on liver and muscle cells and stays outside the cell.
Three subunits (α, β, γ). The activated receptor makes the α subunit release GDP and bind GTP; α–GTP then moves away.
Activated by α–GTP; converts ATP into cyclic AMP (cAMP).
Many cAMP molecules are made, carrying the signal inside the cell.
Activated by cAMP; starts a phosphorylation cascade (kinases add phosphate groups to other enzymes).
The cascade activates glycogen phosphorylase, which breaks glycogen down to glucose. In the liver, glucose is released into the blood.
One adrenaline molecule → many cAMP → many active enzymes → a huge number of glucose molecules.

g.text: 1 adrenaline → many cAMP → many active enzymes → millions of glucose: AMPLIFICATION
